summary: Retires the TLV mechanism in the Associated Channel Header of the MPLS Generic Associated Channel. No channel type uses ACH TLVs, and handling them in hardware causes problems on the fast path, so this document updates RFC 5586 to remove them.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC removes the optional TLV construct from the MPLS Generic Associated Channel. It says G-ACh messages must not be preceded by ACH TLVs and deletes the related IANA registry.

subtitle: Retires ACH TLVs from the MPLS Generic Associated Channel and removes their registry.

tldr.problem: No defined Associated Channel Type used ACH TLVs, and their variable formats complicate hardware processing.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC deletes the ACH TLV definition, prohibits G-ACh messages from being preceded by one, and removes registry entries.
tldr.outcome: ACH TLVs are retired and RFC 5586 is updated.

facts.label: Defined ACH Channel Types at publication

today: RFC 7026 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5586. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 7026.

sections.title: Why ACH TLVs Are Retired
sections.content:
RFC 5586 generalized the Associated Channel Header for messages associated with MPLS sections, label-switching paths, and pseudowires. It defined ACH TLVs to carry additional context before the G-ACh message.

At the time of this RFC, none of the 18 defined ACH Channel Types allowed those TLVs. The RFC also says variable TLV formats and lengths are difficult to process in hardware.
sections.plainLanguage: No defined channel type used the optional TLVs, and their variable sizes complicated hardware processing. The RFC removes the construct.

sections.title: Changes to the G-ACh
sections.content:
Section 3 of RFC 5586, which defined ACH TLVs, is deleted. References to ACH TLVs in Section 4 are to be disregarded.

A G-ACh message MUST NOT be preceded by an ACH TLV. The RFC does not address TLVs used elsewhere or proposals to place them within or after ACH messages.
sections.plainLanguage: The TLV definition is removed, and a G-ACh message must not have an ACH TLV before it. Other TLV uses are outside this RFC.

sections.title: Registry and Security Effects
sections.content:
IANA deleted the Associated Channel Header TLV Registry and removed the TLV Follows column from the Pseudowire Associated Channel Types registry. The document says it has no manageability impact because no channel types allowed TLVs.

Removing the feature may have a marginal positive security effect because TLVs could carry false information or enlarge G-ACh messages. The RFC otherwise identifies no security implications.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry and its related column are removed. The RFC says the change may reduce opportunities to add false or oversized information.
